how: We read the website of every Chicago wedding florist listed on Lazo (294 listings, 229 sites reachable) and set aside the ones that are not really in the wedding business: same-day delivery shops, flower preservation studios, a gold-dipped rose gift company, a balloon-arch business, a micro-wedding venue, and decor rental houses. What is left is a shortlist of vendors who say clearly what they do, show their work, and tell you how they work. Verified Lazo vendors come first. Nobody paid to be here, and this is not a ranking: Lazo ranks only on reviews from couples who booked.
ask: What is local in my month? Illinois growers go quiet from November to April, so a winter wedding means imported stems and the price that comes with them.
Is there a minimum, and does it change between the city and the suburbs?
Do you install and strike at the venue, and what does the venue require for hanging pieces?

picks.name: Bright + Bloom Floral Design
picks.blurb: Founded in 2020 as Blush Blooms & Co. and since renamed, Bright + Bloom is a Shorewood studio doing fully custom wedding florals with delivery and on-site installation, plus a self-set-up option of pre-arranged pieces for pickup for couples who want flexibility.

picks.name: An English Garden Wedding & Event Florals
picks.blurb: Kim's full-service shop in Mokena has done wedding florals for over 30 years and counts thousands of weddings, with its own designers and delivery crew. Event rentals come from the same shop, and the first consultation is free.

picks.name: Anthony Gowder Designs
picks.blurb: Anthony and Stephanie Gowder started their Chicago event company after meeting at a small floral shop, and it is now past 25 years. Full-service design that treats flowers, lighting, furnishings and fabric as one picture, with production and coordination handled in house.

picks.name: Schultz Florist Weddings and Events
picks.blurb: A third-generation, family-owned flower shop in New Lenox serving Chicagoland for over 60 years, with weddings as its signature. Karen Johnson coordinates weddings with 27 years of design behind her, and the retail shop keeps regular hours if you want to drop in.

picks.name: Romee Willow Florals
picks.blurb: Jori Foreman, a painter by training, leads this Logan Square studio that calls its aesthetic unconventional and has designed hundreds of weddings since 2011. Full service covers up to three locations, installations and chuppahs, and leftover flowers are composted or donated to nursing homes.

picks.name: Avant Gardenia
picks.blurb: A Wheaton florist whose owner learned the trade over nearly a decade in her grandparents' flower shop, and whose sole focus is weddings and events. The site states its minimums, $7,500 for suburban weddings and $15,000 in Chicago, May through December, and the designer you meet is the one who runs your event.

picks.name: Elena's Garden Floral Design and Event Planning
picks.blurb: Carla's team combines floral design with wedding planning, a family passion traced to a grandmother named Elena, with over 15 years of producing events. Chicago-based, with a consultation form that promises a reply within hours.

picks.name: Life in Bloom
picks.blurb: A Chicago luxury event design company and WBENC-certified women-owned business that has spent over a decade on suspended decor, floral installations, ceremony design and custom bars, with a crew of more than twenty artisans. It takes a limited number of events each season.

picks.name: Oliver Dogwood Floral Co
picks.blurb: Tiffany Schimmerling opened Oliver Dogwood in the West Loop in 2005 after years at Chicago flower shops, and prints starting prices: bridal bouquets from $225, centerpieces from $150, with a $10,000 minimum for weddings.

picks.name: Branching Out Event Florist - Chicago
picks.blurb: Christine Boulton turned to flowers 15 years ago after 30 years writing about weddings, and runs Branching Out from West Dundee with co-owner Kevin. The team sets up from the entry to the dessert table and returns to make it disappear, for weddings of 30 or 300.

picks.name: Printer's Row Floral Studio
picks.blurb: Funky floral design for cool people, in the studio's own words, from the South Loop. Prices are on the site: full-service weddings from $3,000, event pieces from $500, and a $390 bouquet-and-boutonniere bundle delivered to City Hall.

picks.name: Saville Flowers
picks.blurb: Don Saville opened the shop in 1942 and it is now in its fourth generation of family ownership, in the same Evanston walls. The style has moved from classic European design to something brighter and modern, with weddings alongside everyday flowers.
